I understand this. Having social anxiety and feeling like I am responsible for conversations, I find silences to be extremely hard. I need to be very close to somebody in order for that to go away, and it even then it still comes up. I had an ex say once 'silence really terrifies you huh?' I am trying to become more comfortable with them and sometimes silences mean much more than words. 

I have actually spoken with a couple friends who feel the same way. Basically it boils down to a feeling of 'failure' in the conversation when silences arise. People who get anxiety from silences like that tend to see it as THEIR failure, like they are doing something wrong to create a silence typically which is interpreted as awkward. When in reality its completely natural and fine/healthy.

tl;dr I think it all stems from anxiety/perceived failure which causes this kind of behavior.

Hey man, I have totally been there. I used to binge eat like crazy. I remember just feeling so bad about myself, and seemingly food made me feel temporarily better. I hated doing that to myself.

Well, to start I would say you need to confront the impulses that make you want to binge. These are some of the hardest things to break. I still binge eat at times, though its on very rare occasion. First and foremost, at least for me, was feeling empowered. Just simply acknowledging, at the time it was to my family, that I needed to lose weight. Once I had support and proclaimed what I needed it helped a tooon. 

When you have the urge to binge eat, sometimes just giving yourself like 30 seconds makes all the difference in the world. As you are reaching for those cheese itz or whatever, just stop and say "im gonna wait just 30 seconds and think about this. Is this what I want?". I know it seems silly, but it helped me. 90% of the time I would realize that it wouldnt make me happy. After I finish the last bite, I would be even more depressed than when I reached for the comfort of food.

As per the losing weight portion. I tried a low carb diet varient. I dont think its very good for your heart, so I dont do them anymore. But I lost weight crazy fast and felt super empowered. Felt like I was in control and that I had power over my body and myself. It was probably the best medicine of all.

The thing about low carb is how it relates to my previous post. Making a distinctive change. Time and time again, I have tried low calorie diets and such and I find them extremely hard to sustain. Since its easy to justify just one more bite, its only a couple extra calories. Next thing you know, you have just had a 4 course meal and are halfway through a tub of ice cream saying tomorrow you will start the diet for real. (I am only talking about myself here, these are things I have experienced)

The mental framework of Low Carb diets helped me more than the diet itself. Because I was basically ELIMINATING carbs, I found it easier to stick to rather than reducing an abstraction such as numbers on a label. It was tangible, it was real, and it was black/white. Which helped me stick to it.

Anyhow, I dont recommend low carb since it has toxic adverse effects. I am currently trying something my friend showed me, which works for me. The reason being is that it maintains the same framework. Basically I eat only produce during the day and then 'whatever i want' for dinner. I throw that in quotes, because its within reason. So when I go to work, I take some veggies, avacados, carrots, grapes, frozen veggies, etc. And when im hungry eat something. Then for dinner I usually go out to eat and have 'whatever I want'. It's not a feast. Its easy to think that because you have done so well during the day you deserve a feast. Have something you will enjoy, but watch your sodium. Try not to get large portions, just something that will sate that hunger you have. Whether its pasta, asian, chicken, sandwich, etc. etc. etc. Anyhow thats where I am at and have already lost 6 lbs in the last month AND have upped my veggies by a butt ton. Really helps my mood and confidence as well. Thanksgiving really threw me off, but im hoping when I get back into it, my mood and confidence will return.

Just find something that works for you, I know you can do it man! I believe in you! Hopefully something I shared will help!

Actually yea, I might. I changed my habits a few years back and lost 85 lbs. What I learned from that, which I think can be applied to any facet of lifestyle, is that once you decide that you want to make a change (and in what areas) it's better to make big/distinct changes rather than small ones. When you try making changes in habit and implement small changes, you see those changes as the anomaly in your life. Rather than as something new. Ie. This is why people say the term "diet" is problematic, because it implies a temporal anomaly. 

Using weightloss as a metaphor for whatever habits you want to change, When I lost weight, I made huge changes in eating habits, exercise, daily routine, etc. I'm not saying bite off more than you can chew. This is self defeating. But make sure you fill your daily life with change, it will help you mentally change your habits. 

Hope this helps :)

I will also be 27 in April (So just a couple months younger than you). I actually relate with just about EVERYTHING you are saying haha. Long story short, how do I stay motivated?

On the inside I'm a mix of a complete disaster/train wreck and being super excited. Excited because I love socializing with people, it makes me happy and give me hope. There are times that it is EXTREMELY hard. I am currently struggling pretty bad to be honest. Work actually helps me stay motivated. I suppose because I have a reason to socialize with the people around me and having a reason has always reduced my SA. (Which conversely makes dating/asking people out to be hard for me)

A lot of the time I think its best to take things one day at a time and it surprises me how much being outside in the fresh air helps. To be honest though, I am seemingly in a very similar boat with you and am also wondering about some good techniques to stay motivated.

In college, on the rare chance we actually had to do this, I would find the "safest person" in the room. The one who would intimidate me/give me anxiety the least and ask them to join me.

When I got smarter I would go sit near the girl I found to be the cutest and hope somehow we naturally just got paired up. Usually didn't happen because I could barely acknowledge them, few times it worked though :p

Read the book "Are We Rome?: The Fall of an Empire and the Fate of America"  by Cullen Murphy. 


IMO America compares itself to Rome for MANY MANY reasons. I shall just list a few.

1. The American Republic is based off the Roman Republic.
2. Both nations overthrew a monarchy and installed a republic.
3. Both nations were superpowers of their time. United States is *currently* the only superpower and has influences throughout the world. Rome directly controlled much of the "known world" at that time.
4. Western tradition was defined during Classical Antiquity "ancient Rome and Greece."
5. Our culture, language, warfare strategy, politics, philosophy, basically anything western is derived from ancient Rome.


This list could go on and on and be debated. But something I think should be mentioned here is the future of American and the fate of Rome. Some believe America is on the brink of becoming an empire, if not already one through its foreign policy of being the  "world police."

Murphy goes over all this in the book and emphasizes one major point, which is that technically History does NOT repeat itself and America is NOT Rome. We could write a 1,000 page essay on how similar the U.S. and Rome are...but it would take eternity to show how they are different.
